name: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Japfa Comfeed: the chick band changes nothing, the terminal margin does
frontmatter.summary: Bapanas replaced the single day-old-chick price with a band whose ceiling repeats the old figure, so no forecast line moves on the 10 November circular. What moves is the valuation: the unsourced terminal margin lift is removed, the peak-earnings multiple legs are cut to a fifth each and the target falls to Rp2,289, still a BUY against Rp1,490. The bear case is below the price.
thesis: The earnings being discounted are nine months already filed: net sales of IDR54,525.0bn, gross profit of IDR11,249.5bn and operating profit of IDR5,179.2bn, on a 20.6% gross margin earned while corn and meal ran above the prior year [S3, F5, F6, F7].

The pack's depreciation line is only a fraction of the charge the LK books — IDR1,140.3bn in the FY2025 fixed-asset note and IDR1,060.9bn in FY2024 — so every multiple built on pack EBITDA is wrong. Restating it lifts FY2025A EBITDA to IDR7,323.9bn and cuts the multiple the shares trade on [S4, F1, F2].

The cash outflow is the finding, not a footnote: the nine months used IDR4,558.1bn in operations and IDR3,879.1bn on fixed assets, and the build is inventory, biological stock and corn advances measured at the balance-sheet date [S3, F26, F44].

The live-bird market is below cost for independent farmers [S9], and the state has answered it by cutting chick supply and expecting prices to recover; October averaged Rp22,000 against the Rp21,000 low [S10, S9]. Both tails are in the distribution.
The target is probability-weighted, not the base case: base Rp2,133, bear Rp1,305 and bull Rp3,586, with the DCF — the primary leg — at Rp1,336 and no terminal margin lift [S0].

catalysts.event: Interim dividend paid, cum 5 November and ex 6 November, declared while the company was borrowing to hold inventory; the test is whether the working capital unwinds before the FY2026 accounts [S6, S3].
Agriculture ministry supervision of integrators tightens; any rule on live-bird pricing or placement quotas reaches the commercial farm, the largest segment, directly [S7, S4].
FY2026 audited accounts due: whether the fourth quarter holds the nine-month margin, whether the inventory and advance build unwinds into cash, and whether Q4 carries the usual true-ups [S3].

blocks.text: **BUY, target Rp2,289 against Rp1,490: total return 63.7%, price upside 53.7%.** The target is the probability-weighted value of three scenarios — base Rp2,133 on 50%, bear Rp1,305 on 25% and bull Rp3,586 on 25% [S0]. The bear sits below the price; the bull is a multiple of it. That shape is the strongest evidence in this report, and the prior version described it backwards.

**What changed, and why the target moved down.** Three corrections, all the red team's. First, the terminal margin lift is gone: the prior version raised the constant-price input about a point above its FY2029E level, an improvement with no source. Held flat, the realised margin fades with the deck's cost path to 17.5% by FY2035E and the DCF is Rp1,336 [S0, deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]. Second, the earnings legs carry a fifth each rather than three tenths and a fifth, because both apply a multiple to FY2025A earnings and the engine rolls the blend at a cost of equity of 17.1% — assuming peak earnings compound at that rate while our own FY2027E EPS of Rp333 is below FY2026E's Rp374 [S0]. Third, the bear is the printed FY2023 trough and the working-capital ratio is the measured one.

**The 10 November circular changes no forecast line.** Bapanas replaced the farm-level chick price with a band — a floor of Rp6,500 beneath a Rp7,000 ceiling a bird, against the Rp7,000 the prior decree set [S8, F30, F31, F32]. The ceiling repeats the old figure, the floor is new, and it lands on the breeding segment — IDR3,541.5bn of FY2025 sales, IDR3,106.3bn in nine months — with the chick moving within the group [S4, S3, F13, F20].

**Why the target is not a peer-median artefact.** Both earnings legs blend a four-observation own-history mean with a five-peer median that changed counterpart when the pack refreshed on 12 November — from CPRO.JK to CPIN.JK — with no company input moving [S0]. Hence a fifth each.

**The restatement that changes every multiple.** The pack's FY2025 depreciation line is well below the charge the fixed-asset note books — IDR1,140.3bn in FY2025 and IDR1,060.9bn in FY2024 [S4, F1, F2]. Restated to the note, the shares trade at 3.7x FY2025A EV/EBITDA and 4.5x on our first forecast year [S0, S4].

**The variant view.** The market pays 4.0x our FY2026E earnings and 4.5x its EBITDA, with a dividend yield of 10.0% [S0]. That is too cheap for a business whose nine-month margin was earned at a higher corn cost than last year's and whose borrowing funds a dated harvest position rather than a loss. The disagreement is not about the industry — the live-bird market is genuinely below smallholder cost [S9] — but about duration: we model the working capital turning and the margin fading to the four-year mean, not to the trough.

Japfa Comfeed is an integrated poultry and animal-protein group. The LK reports six segments, whose FY2025 external sales were IDR24,513.8bn in the commercial farm, IDR15,786.7bn in animal feed, IDR10,647.8bn in processing and consumer products, IDR5,137.2bn in aquaculture, IDR3,541.5bn in poultry breeding and IDR2,300.4bn in trading; exports were IDR1,339.6bn of the total [S4, F9, F10, F11, F12, F13, F14, F15].

Over the nine months to September 2026 the commercial farm booked IDR20,728.4bn, feed IDR15,662.8bn, processing and consumer products IDR9,831.5bn, aquaculture IDR4,381.3bn, breeding IDR3,106.3bn and trading IDR2,036.7bn [S3, F16–F21]. The farm is largest and breeding smallest, which is why the chick band is a segment question before a consolidated one; feed is second and the farm's internal supplier, so the corn and meal links reach both [S3, S8].

Two structural facts carry into the valuation. The company owns a national feed-mill footprint with corn dryers at harvest, which is why inventory here is strategic working capital [S2, S3]. And the vaccine subsidiary was sold in September 2026 to Japfa Pte. Ltd. and Bionovus Pte. Ltd., under common control, for gross proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn [S3, F29].

The Indonesian poultry chain is a set of integrators surrounded by independent smallholders.
Integrators own the feed mill, the breeding line and often the slaughterhouse; the independent farmer
buys chicks and feed and sells live birds into a market where the farm-gate price is set daily and is
volatile. Because feed is the largest cost in a broiler and corn the largest input in feed, the
integrator earns a spread between the corn it buys and the chicken it sells, and the two move for
different reasons. That is why the business swings between a thin margin and a fat one, and why a
mid-cycle margin is the right anchor.

Demand is staples with a cyclical price on top: poultry is the cheapest widely available animal protein and consumption per head rises with income [S2]. But the producer price clears daily and has swung both ways this year — a live-bird recovery to Rp22,000 a kilogram in October against the Rp21,000 the farmers' association quoted in early October, after the ministry directed integrators to cut day-old-chick final stock by at least 10% effective 19 October 2026 [S9, S10, F35, F50, F51]. That cut is the most important industry fact of this revision: it supports the commercial farm and the processing chain directly.

The cost side is the deck: corn at US$215/t for FY2026E against US$173/t last year, meal at US$411/t against US$321/t and up again to US$450/t [S0, deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]. **The base takes that forward cost path, not the spot quotes**: it charges four fifths of each deck move into cost of goods sold, and a spot-holds path — this year's corn and meal carried flat at US$175/t and US$361/t — is the bull tail, not the base [S0]. Four fifths rather than the nine tenths a single nine-month comparison would allow, because one period cannot separate pass-through from carried harvest inventory [S0, S3, S4]. CPIN.JK charges a lower rate on the same template; on a tenth of the ration bill the gap is worth roughly a percentage point of gross margin, reflecting JPFA's larger processing share [S2, S4]. Terminal growth of 4.0% is our own input, not the deck's whole-economy real GDP growth of 5.29% [S0, deck.macro.gdp_real_id], and the deck carries the rupiah from Rp16,448/USD to Rp18,350/USD against an imported meal bill [S0, S4].

Policy is an active variable, reaching the integrator from both ends: supply rules on the farm, subsidised corn for smallholders on the feed spread, and now the 10 November chick band — a floor of Rp6,500 beneath a Rp7,000 ceiling a bird, plus a meat reference price of Rp25,000 and a corn ceiling of Rp5,800 [S7, S5, S10, S8]. Competition is a handful of integrated groups plus a long tail of mills; Japfa's cost and distribution moat rests on national feed-mill coverage, corn drying at harvest and a branded processed-chicken business, while supplier power sits in corn and meal and rivalry clears through the live-bird price [S0, S2, S5].

Revenue is built from the filing, not from a growth assumption: nine-month net sales of IDR54,525.0bn annualise to IDR73,696.8bn at a flat fourth quarter — growth of 21.4% — then decelerate to 8.0% as this year's input-cost push is not repeated [S3, F5, deck.agri.corn].

The margin is the load-bearing assumption and it is the witnessed one. Gross profit of IDR11,249.5bn on that sales base is a gross margin of 20.6%, what the filing prints, and the cost links are calibrated to deliver it rather than assumed to [S3, F6]. Operating margin is 9.5% against 10.2% in the record year — a step down of less than a percentage point and a rounding artefact of holding the nine-month gross margin over one quarter at unchanged prices, not a separate assumption [S4, S3, F6]. Depreciation is the restated charge in the fixed-asset note, IDR1,140.3bn in FY2025, not the fraction the pack carries, so every cash cost here is built on the corrected number [S4, F1].

Cash flow is where the story is uncomfortable and we do not smooth it. The nine-month statement shows operating outflow of IDR4,558.1bn after interest of IDR881.9bn and tax of IDR717.0bn, against capital expenditure of IDR3,879.1bn plus land of IDR154.2bn; the financing side is disclosed item by item — divestment proceeds of IDR1,766.3bn against a gross transaction value of IDR1,807.4bn, the IDR1,000.0bn of shareholder-loan repayments received on that divestment, and dividends of IDR1,620.9bn [S3, F29, F36–F43]. FY2026E free cash flow of IDR-6,557.6bn is struck after a working-capital build of IDR7,789.0bn at 25.6% of revenue, and is *less* negative than the nine-month arithmetic annualised because the fourth quarter carries neither harvest build nor release [S3, F26, F44]. The red team asked whether the deficit was understated by several trillion rupiah: it reconciles line by line.

Debt is the other half: the prior year end carried a large bond in current liabilities, since repaid, so the headline rise is part refinancing, part new borrowing, and we carry the witnessed net increase into the first forecast year [S3, F22, F23, F24]. At IDR18,338.4bn of net debt and 2.2x EBITDA the balance sheet is comfortable against the FY2023 trough but no longer near net cash; finance costs of IDR788.7bn show it [S0, S3, F28]. Capital expenditure of IDR5,623.1bn, or 7.6% of sales against 4.6% in FY2025, falls to 3.0% in the terminal year — depreciation plus growth, not a haircut. The dividend follows the declared policy, not the peak payout: Rp150 against Rp230 declared for FY2025 [S0, S3, S4, S6].

Earnings quality, through the house screens, and this is where the red team was right to push. The accruals ratio — net profit less operating cash flow over average total assets — is roughly a fifth for the current year, above the threshold, and it is inventory: stock of IDR14,355.3bn against IDR9,599.6bn at the prior year end is close to twice nine-month cost of sales of IDR43,275.5bn [S3, F26, F44, F46, F8, F36]. Optics-class, on four grounds: the build is a physical inventory and advances position disclosed in the notes, not a receivable from an affiliate; cost of goods sold reconciles to the prior-year comparative at IDR34,389.5bn with no change of scope; no receivable outgrows revenue and no borrowing cost is capitalised; and the third quarter is unaudited [S3, F45, F46]. The risk still goes into the bear as an inventory write-down inside the margin shock. Two further items: the vaccine disposal was a common-control transaction with the tax on the difference charged to equity, so the equity credit is the residual and reported profit never saw the headline proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn [S3, F29]; and the disposal plus the shareholder-loan repayment closed on 29 September 2026, retiring a slice of net debt within the period valued [S3, F29, F42]. The IDX regime screen is clean and there is no manipulation-class finding [S2]. Related-party payables are IDR384.7bn, down from a much larger prior-year figure, so the gravity test does not fire [S3, F27].

The method set fits because this is an asset-heavy, working-capital-heavy integrator whose earnings swing with a commodity spread: a discounted cash flow prices the asset base and the cycle, a multiple cross-check prices what the market pays for those earnings at a point in it [S0]. The red team's challenge — that the multiple legs apply a cycle-average multiple to peak earnings — is right. The engine applies peer and own-history multiples to the last actual year, with no forward-multiple option, so a DCF-heavy weighting is the honest fix: DCF 60%, P/E 20% and EV/EBITDA 20% against an even split, which lowers the target because the cash-flow value is the lowest of the three [S0].

The cost of capital is built rather than asserted: the deck's rupiah ten-year at 7.4%, equity premium 4.2%, Indonesia country risk premium 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.7x from an industry 0.9x at a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.1x, giving a cost of equity of 17.1% and a WACC of 12.0% [S0]. The cost of equity sits above the house band because the balance sheet is levered at about one times the market capitalisation; the WACC does not, and we have not adjusted it.

The primary method discounts free cash flow from the 30 September balance-sheet date, so the stub year carries only the final quarter, and exits on terminal growth of 4.0% with a terminal value share of 50.5% [S0] — high, as for a capital-intensive business, and the honest weakness here. The implied exit multiple — terminal value over FY2035E EBITDA, both in the tables — is the test the house card demands and it fails: it lies below the 6.7x the EV/EBITDA cross-check applies [S0]. Run at that exit multiple instead of terminal growth, the same cash flows would value the shares above the multiple cross-checks — which is why those cross-checks sit where they do, and why the report believes the cash-flow number and gives it three fifths of the weight [S0]. The terminal margin lift is now fixed in the model rather than disclosed: the constant-price margin is held flat from FY2029E into perpetuity at 20.4%, with no lift [S4, S3, deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]. Removing it is the largest single reason the target moves to Rp2,289 [S0].

The divergence is the finding, stated rather than buried: the DCF gives Rp1,336, the P/E cross-check Rp2,907, up 117.6%, and the EV/EBITDA cross-check Rp2,836, up 112.3% [S0]; both flags are answered in the assumptions file. The P/E applies 8.5x to an earnings base the market capitalises at 4.0x, and the EV/EBITDA applies 6.7x against a market 4.5x — an equal average of the peer median and JPFA's own four-observation history, as the published target was built [S0].

The sensitivity that matters is the gross margin and, behind it, the corn and meal path: a point of operating margin is worth materially more than a point of discount rate, which is why the evidence is spent on the margin rather than on arguing the WACC [S0].

**Live bird and the smallholder squeeze — high likelihood, high impact.** In early October the farmers' association put the farm-gate price at Rp21,000 a kilogram, below its members' cost of production, and warned of closures [S9, F35]; after the ministry's supply cut the October average recovered to Rp22,000 [S10, F51]. A tenth on that price is roughly a twenty-fifth of group sales at the commercial farm's share, so it is the fastest way to lose the nine-month margin. The bear assumes the October recovery does not hold; the bull assumes it does.

**Policy intervention in the integrator model — medium likelihood, high impact.** The ministry is tightening supervision while distributing subsidised corn to smallholders, and ordered a chick final-stock cut of 10% effective 19 October 2026 [S7, S10, F50]. Placement caps, a live-bird floor or a corn channel outside the integrator reach all land on the farm or the feed spread.

**The chick-price band — low likelihood, low impact.** The November circular holds the farm-level chick at the prior decree's figure and adds a floor of Rp6,500 beneath a Rp7,000 ceiling [S8, F30, F31]. Direct exposure is the breeding segment's external sales while the farm is supplied from the group's own line, so the band redistributes between segments rather than changing consolidated profit [S3, S2, F13].

**Input cost and currency — medium likelihood, medium impact.** The deck has corn and meal rising into this year, meal again later, and the rupiah weaker [S0, S4]. Nine-month evidence says the company passes it on, but pass-through holds only while demand holds, and a weaker rupiah raises the imported meal bill without raising the chicken price in the same month [S0, S4].

**Balance sheet and liquidity — medium likelihood, medium impact.** An inventory position is funded with short-term bank debt that must be rolled [S3, F22]. Not a solvency event, but a squeeze can force liquidation at the wrong point in the harvest calendar.

**Governance and related parties — low likelihood, high impact.** The vaccine business went to group entities under common control [S3, F29]. Not that the transaction was unfair — proceeds and equity treatment are disclosed — but that the group's ability to transact with the listed company is an option on value we cannot size.

**Scenarios.** Both tails shock the same four drivers — gross margin, corn, meal and net borrowing — by mirrored amounts, symmetric in construction and not only in narrative [S0]. The bear runs the FY2023 trough gross margin of 14.7% and operating margin of 4.0% inside one margin shock that also carries the inventory write-down, and lifts the deck's corn and meal path by the reciprocal of the bull's markdown on the same two inputs, so the two tails are mirror images rather than one path plus a discount; net borrowing rises by exactly what the bull lowers [S0, S9]. The bull is the spot-holds path — corn at US$175/t and meal at US$361/t, held flat against the deck's forward curve — the one the base does not assume, with the October recovery holding, a margin recovery and the mirror debt relief [S10, S0]. The asymmetry is deliberate and sourced: recovery to the record 21.7% is a smaller move than a fall to the trough [S0, S4]. Base half, a quarter each tail.

The bear at Rp1,305 is below the Rp1,490 price, and the rebuilt value now matches the words the published note used [S0]. The bull at Rp3,586 is close to double, the base at Rp2,133 carries the weight, and the probability-weighted figure is Rp2,289.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Two quarters of margin below the nine-month level; the farm-gate price holding October's level through a full placement cycle; a rule capping placements or setting a live-bird floor; enforcement of the chick band or corn ceiling at the gate; inventory unwinding with cash turning positive; and any further related-party transaction [S5, S7, S3, S8, S10].

Ownership is resolved from the register, not the pack: Japfa Pte. Ltd. holds 55.4% and is both controlling and majority shareholder, the public holds 43.8%, treasury stock the small residual [S2, F48, F49]; the pack's insider and free-float figures do not add up, the annual report's register does, and it is the one we use [S2]. No share-pledge disclosure appears in the filing we archived — a gap in our evidence, not a clean finding.

Related parties are disclosed and material. Trade payables to related parties were IDR384.7bn at the end of September, down from a much larger prior-year balance, and the vaccine subsidiary went to Japfa Pte. Ltd. and Bionovus Pte. Ltd. for gross proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn, with the restructuring difference in equity and a shareholder loan of IDR1,000.0bn repaid on the divestment [S3, F27, F29, F42]. A disclosed disposal beats an undisclosed one, but it is still a channel for value to move to the controlling group, and the size is not small against a year's profit [S3, F8].

The FY2025 accounts are audited by KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, a member firm of Ernst & Young Global Limited, signed under the registered public accountant rules; the interims are unaudited as for every IDX issuer, and fourth quarters carry true-ups [S4, S3]. The distribution record is consistent: Rp230 a share declared for FY2025 and an interim declared in October, cum 5 November, ex 6 November 2026, payable 12 November 2026 [S0, S6]. The interim is paid while the company borrows: either confidence that the inventory unwinds or an upstreaming of cash, and the disclosure does not settle which.

ESG exposure sits in biosecurity and the smallholder relationship: disease is the existential operational risk, and the animal-health operations that mitigated it have been sold to the controlling group, while the integrator-versus-smallholder question is the live political issue and this company is the integrator [S2, S3, S7].

The dated events are the interim payment in the second week of November, the FY2026 audited accounts at the end of February and whatever follows the ministry's integrator review [S6, S3, S7]. Monitoring: quarterly operating margin against the nine-month level; the farm-gate live-bird price; the chick price against the band and whether either end is enforced; inventory and advances; gross debt and its maturity mix; corn and meal against the deck; and any related-party disclosure [S3, S5, S0, S8].

We would revisit the rating on a sustained margin below the nine-month level, a policy rule that changes integrator economics, or a related-party transaction moving value away from the listed company; and raise it on evidence the working-capital build unwinds into cash while the margin holds [S3, S5, S7].

bear.narrative: A repeat of FY2023, which is the trough the record actually printed: gross margin 14.68% and operating margin 3.97% [S0, S4]. The live-bird market is already below cost -- independent farmers put the farm-gate price at Rp21,000- 22,000/kg against their own cost of production in October [S9, F35, F51] -- and the commercial farm is the largest segment at F16 [S4, S3]. The ministry's DOC cut is not enough to clear the surplus, feed repricing stops as placements fall, corn and meal carry a further cost step, and the margin gives back the 2026 gain and the 2024-25 recovery together. The 2026 inventory and advance build is written down inside the margin shock rather than unwound at cost, so borrowing rises instead of falling. The shocks are mirrored with the bull on every driver: the margin step is the FY2023 trough repeat, the deck inputs are stepped the opposite way, and the funding cost is the working-capital build funded rather than released.

bull.narrative: Spot costs hold, which is the case the deck's own tape makes possible and the one missing from the prior version: corn at 175.39 and soybean meal at 360.57 on spot against 214.57 and 411.00 in the deck for FY2026E-FY2027E, a fifth and an eighth below [deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]. Held through the explicit period, that is worth about 4pp of gross margin at the 80% pass-through, and it is the whole of the cost-side shock here. On the revenue side the ministry has cut final DOC stock to rebalance supply, effective 19 October 2026, and the live-bird price averaged Rp22,000/kg in October against the Rp21,000/kg the same article quotes for the low [S10, F50, F51]; the commercial farm is the largest segment, so the recovery reaches group profit directly [S9, S4]. The VSN proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn and the IDR1,000.0bn shareholder loan repaid [S3, F29] reduce debt rather than fund a larger build.

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is built from the filing, not assumed: nine months to 30 September 2026 delivered net sales of IDR 54,525.0bn against IDR 43,104.4bn in the same nine months of 2025, growth of 26.5% [S3, F5]. The fourth quarter is carried at the third quarter's own run-rate of IDR 19,169.9bn rather than grossed up, because the 2025 fourth quarter was itself an end-of-year step (IDR 17,611.4bn against the IDR 13,149.3bn second quarter) whose repeat is not evidenced in any source; that gives about IDR 73,695bn, or +21.4% on FY2025's IDR 60,715.8bn [S3, S0]. The growth is concentrated in animal feed, up by two fifths, and in the commercial farm, up by a fifth, on the segment note [S3, F16, F17]. FY2027E steps down to 8.0%: the deck's corn and soybean meal are flat in 2027, so the input-cost push that carried 2026 feed prices is not repeated, and volume growth at the deck's long-run Indonesian rate plus a point of share gain is what remains [d.agri.corn, d.agri.soymeal, m.gdp_real_id]. The following years taper to 7.0%, 6.5% and 6.0% as the protein market matures; the 4.5% long run sits above the deck's 3.28% consumer inflation because per-capita protein consumption in Indonesia is still rising, and below every explicit year.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the witnessed nine-month margin and faded to a through-cycle level, not held at the top of the printed range. The input is the margin at the FY2025A deck input prices; the two cost links then charge the deck's own cost path at the 80% pass-through set below, so FY2026E reproduces the filed gross margin of 20.63% (gross profit IDR 11,249.5bn on net sales IDR 54,525.0bn [S3, F5, F6]) by construction. From FY2027E the input is cut so the modelled margin fades to 19.90%, 19.00%, 18.50% and 18.50% by FY2029E, and holds 18.50% into perpetuity. The anchor is measured, not cautious: the four-year printed gross margins were 15.69%, 14.68%, 20.10% and 21.73% [S0, S4], a mean of 18.05%, but those margins were earned at a mean weighted input cost index of 108.4 (0.26 x corn + 0.13 x soymeal on the deck's own actuals: corn 273.2/221.9/166.9/172.6, soybean meal 488.3/481.9/369.0/321.2 [deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]) and the deck's FY2026E index is 109.2 -- the same cost level, so 18.05% is already the cost-adjusted mid-cycle. A linear fit of the four printed margins plus 9M2026 on that index gives 18.45% at the FY2026E cost, which is the number we hold. We do not carry 20.63% for five years and 21.41% in perpetuity, which would capitalise the second-best year in the record at a mid-range cost; nor do we go to the 15.8% the same fit implies at the deck's FY2035E cost, because the company reprices feed within the year and the deck's rising cost path is a forecast, not an actual [S3, S4]. The constant-price margin is therefore held flat from FY2029E at 20.36% into perpetuity, with no lift: the red team is right that the prior version raised it to 21.34% in the long run, a point of unsourced structural improvement, and that correction is now applied. The realised margin consequently fades with the deck's own cost path rather than being held at 18.50% to FY2035E, and the base target no longer depends on the lift [S0, S3, deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Corn is the largest single input in poultry feed, and feed is the group's second-largest external segment and the internal supplier to the commercial farm [S2, S4, F9, F10]. We set the exposed share of consolidated cost of goods sold at 26%. This is an analyst estimate, not a company disclosure: the LK does not publish a raw-material composition of cost of goods sold, so the number is reasoned from the feed segment's share of external sales and from the standard broiler ration rather than quoted. It is deliberately the smaller side of the plausible range, so the linked margin is not levered to our own guess [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Eighty per cent, lowered from ninety: the four-year record does not support full pass-through. Re-pricing FY2023 to FY2024 at 90% pass-through explains 0.76pp of the 5.42pp gross-margin recovery even though corn fell 24.8% and soybean meal 23.4% on the deck actuals, so the realised pass-through on that move was nearer 30%; from FY2022 to FY2023 the margin fell 1.01pp while costs fell 10.5%, the wrong sign for a high pass-through. We hold 80% rather than the historical-implied rate because the nine-month 2026 actual is direct evidence that the 2026 cost move was absorbed: gross margin 20.63% against 20.22% in 9M2025 while the deck's corn rose 24.3% [S3 p.6, deck.agri.corn]. The 20-point gap to CPIN.JK's 0.60 on the same template reflects JPFA's processing and consumer segments, which reprice on the shelf rather than on the ration [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Soybean meal at 13% of consolidated cost of goods sold, half the corn weight, reflecting its smaller share of the broiler and layer ration than corn's energy component [S2, S4]. Like the corn share this is an analyst estimate from the feed formulation rather than a disclosed composition; the LK publishes segment sales and results, not input tonnage or cost [S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Eighty per cent, the same rate and the same evidence as the corn link: the four-year margin-to-cost relationship implies incomplete pass-through while the nine-month 2026 actual shows the 2026 move absorbed [S3, deck.agri.soymeal]. Set equal to the corn link because the feed book is repriced on total ration cost, not input by input.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the filing rather than the data pack: selling and marketing expense of IDR 2,482.9bn plus general and administrative expense of IDR 3,576.8bn on net sales of IDR 54,525.0bn is 11.11% for the nine months to September 2026 [S3]. FY2025 was 11.60% on the same items, so the ratio is falling with scale, which is what a distribution-heavy feed business does when volumes rise. We carry 11.14% flat, the witnessed ratio rounded to the level that reproduces the nine-month operating margin of 9.50% once other income and other expenses (a net IDR 7.9bn charge in the nine months) are left out of the model [S3, F7].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK, not taken from the data pack: Note 13 charges IDR 1,140.3bn of fixed-asset depreciation in FY2025 (IDR 1,060.9bn in FY2024), against the IDR 325.3bn the data pack carries, which is the direct-method cash-flow artefact the house rule warns about [S4, F1, F2, S0]. FY2025 is 1.88% of revenue. The right-of-use charge (IDR 112.9bn in FY2025) is NOT included in the restated fact and therefore not in this ratio; the model's EBITDA is consequently about 1.5% below a total-D&A EBITDA. The forecast holds the fixed-asset charge at the FY2025 ratio and eases it slowly as the elevated 2026 capital programme completes and the asset base grows faster than the charge [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is the witnessed run-rate: capital expenditure of IDR 4,162.3bn in the nine months to September 2026 equals 7.63% of nine-month sales, and we carry the full 7.63% for the year because no source shows the programme slowing in the fourth quarter [S0, S3]. That spend is named: a new hatchery at Berau in East Kalimantan, the Pemalang 2 slaughterhouse, rebuilds of the Palembang and Makassar farms and a grandparent-stock farm at Tanjung Bintang [S2]. It then steps back to 5.5% and 4.8% as the programme completes, above the FY2025 actual of 4.6% [S4, S0]. The long run is 3.0%, not 4.6%: in a steady state capex equals depreciation plus growth in the asset base, which is 1.78% of revenue of D&A [S4, F1] plus 1.21% for 4% growth on the model's FY2035E net fixed assets of 30.2% of revenue, giving 2.99%. The filing's fixed assets of IDR14,995.1bn plus right-of-use assets of IDR244.6bn against FY2025 revenue of IDR60,715.8bn are 25.1% of revenue [S4], which gives 2.78% on the same arithmetic; that ratio is struck on the peak-margin revenue base, so we use the terminal-year asset base [S4, S3]. Holding 4.6% of revenue forever against 1.78% D&A would imply capital intensity rising without limit, which no source supports.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The FY2026E ratio is the witnessed one: inventories rose from IDR 9,599.6bn at 31 December 2025 to IDR 14,355.3bn at 30 September 2026, with biological inventories and advances for corn also up, which took operating working capital from 18.2% of FY2025 sales to 25.6% of the annualised nine-month base [S3, F26, F44, S0]. Biological inventories of IDR2,454.4bn, biological assets of IDR1,957.4bn and advances of IDR1,525.6bn are the lines that moved besides the stock, and trade payables fell from IDR3,706.9bn to IDR2,513.8bn on the related-party settlement, so the build is 7.4 points of revenue, not the 7 points a bare inventory change implies [S3]. That build is the reason the group borrowed IDR7,555bn more in the nine months while still reporting a profit, and it is funded in the model by the same net borrowing [S3, F22, F23]. FY2026E carries the measured 30 September ratio rather than a round 24.5%, so the model's year-end working capital equals the balance already struck at 30 September and the fourth quarter carries no further build and no release; the nine-month cash flow is therefore in the year, not deferred out of it [S3, F36]. We then normalise to 22.0% and 20.0% by 2030 rather than back to 18.2%, because biological assets and the corn advance book have grown structurally with the farm footprint and the company now dries corn itself [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 21.8%, between the 21.9% effective rate of FY2025 [S4] and the 21.5% of the nine months [S3]: income tax of IDR 971.8bn on pre-tax profit of IDR 4,521.2bn is 21.5% for 9M2026, and we take the higher audited-year rate because Q4 true-ups have historically lifted it. It is the statutory rate less small permanent differences and we do not assume it falls.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 8.0%, reconciled between the witnessed average and the marginal rate, because the debt mix changed inside the year. Finance costs of IDR 788.7bn in the nine months on average gross debt of about IDR 15.6tn give 6.8% [S3, F28], but that stock still carried the fixed-rate Rp5.83tn bond that was repaid; short-term bank loans rose from IDR 2,920.9bn to IDR 12,410.4bn and now price off the deck's 5.75% policy rate plus a spread, roughly 8.5-9.0% [S3, F22, m.bi_rate]. We forecast 8.0% as the average over the explicit years as the cheap bond rolls off -- between the witnessed 6.8% and the 9.45% marginal rate the WACC uses, which is the rate on new debt, not the average on the stock [S3].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 2.0%, from finance income of IDR 69.3bn in the nine months on an average cash balance of about IDR 4.1tn [S3]. The company holds most of its liquidity in current accounts and short-term deposits, so the yield sits well below the policy rate and we do not raise it.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the witnessed increase: gross debt went from IDR 11,862.1bn at 31 December 2025 to IDR 19,417.2bn at 30 September 2026, of which IDR 5,831.6bn is the bond that was replaced and the balance is the working-capital and capital-expenditure funding the cash-flow statement shows [S3, F22, F23, F24, S0]. It is not an assumption; it is the balance sheet. From FY2027E the gross debt is held flat rather than repaid: the prior version retired IDR1,500bn a year, and on that path the modelled cash balance went negative from FY2028E, which is not a forecast anyone believes of a company with an undrawn working-capital book -- if free cash after the programme and the dividend does not cover a repayment, the debt is rolled, not repaid. Holding it flat keeps the modelled cash positive through FY2035E and takes no credit in the DCF for deleveraging, which the cash-flow method does not see anyway. No rights issue is assumed, because none is announced [S3, S4, F22].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. Other income and other expenses are roughly offsetting in both the audited year (IDR 287.6bn of other income against IDR 251.1bn of other expenses) and the nine months (IDR 329.3bn against IDR 337.1bn), so there is no recurring non-operating credit to carry and no charge to add back [S4, S3].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 9.0%, the witnessed nine-month rate rather than the FY2025 6.5%: minorities took IDR 318.0bn of the IDR 3,549.4bn profit in the nine months to September 2026 [S3, F8], and the minority-heavy feed and farm joint ventures' share rises with the farm segment that now leads the mix. Using the most recent period's rate rather than a blend of the two is the accurate choice, not the cautious one.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Forty per cent of earnings, which is what the FY2025 declaration was: IDR 140 a share against EPS of IDR 344 is 40.7% [S0, S4]. The FY2026 interim of IDR 90 a share (IDR 1.05tn, cum 5 November, paid 12 November) is 26% of our FY2026E EPS on its own, so a final payment takes the year to the same ratio [S6]. We do not carry the 52.5% three-year average of cash paid to the prior year's profit, because that series mixes the dates and overstates policy; we do not cut it either, since the company has paid a dividend in every year of the record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. Shares outstanding were 11,627.7m for FY2022-FY2025 and 11,704.9m at 30 September 2026, and the company has not announced a rights issue or buyback; the small rise is share-based payment, which we do not model [S0, S3]. The thesis registry carries a rights issue as a kill criterion precisely because none is expected.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4.0% nominal rupiah: the deck's long-run Indonesian consumer inflation is 3.28% and poultry protein consumption per head is still below the regional average, which is worth about a point of real growth on a mature base [m.cpi_id, S2]. It is below every explicit-year revenue growth rate and below the 5% cap, so the model decelerates into perpetuity rather than stepping up.

challenges.challenge: The +8.0% target (2,619 published on 6 November to 2,829) is attributed to the 12 November pack refresh, but the only input that moved is the peer median. 7.234x in the prior version became 8.50x, and 8.50 is exactly the average of the unchanged own-history mean 10.109x and a peer median that went from 4.359x (CPRO) to 6.886x (CPIN) - a median picking a different one of three peers, not new information about the company. The EV/EBITDA leg moved 6.42x to 6.73x the same way. No before/after method table is given, so a reader cannot see that the whole increase is this re-ranking, and cannot tell whether the published 2,619 was the base case or the weighted target.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now names the median in each version, states that the published target was the base-case figure and not the probability-weighted one, and shows the peer table. The multiple legs are cut to a fifth each because the median re-ranked from CPRO.JK (4.359x P/E, 4.88x EV/EBITDA) to CPIN.JK (6.886x P/E, 5.14x EV/EBITDA) with no company input moving; the DCF is 60% of the blend and unchanged at 1,336.

challenges.challenge: Both earnings legs are struck on peak FY2025 earnings and then grown at COE. The P/E leg is 8.5 x FY2025A EPS of 342.0 (4,004/11,704.9) = 2,907 and the EV/EBITDA leg is 6.73 x FY2025A EBITDA of 7,323.9 less net debt 14,800.9, minorities 1,620.2, plus investments 290.4 = 2,836. The base target then applies (1 + COE 17.08%) to the whole blend, which on the 50% earnings share assumes earnings compound at 17% - while the model own FY2027E net profit is 3,883, 10.8% BELOW the FY2026E 4,352, and EPS falls with it. That roll is worth about IDR330 a share, 13% of the base target, and it contradicts the forecast underneath it.
challenges.answer: The engine applies multiples to LTM earnings and offers no forward-multiple basis, so the fix is weighting, not recomputation: DCF 60%, P/E 20%, EV/EBITDA 20% against the industry even split, which drops the base target to 2,133 on a DCF of 1,336. The report states that the roll at COE 17.08% assumes COE compounding while FY2027E EPS of 333.0 is below FY2026E's 374.3, and the weighting note records why.

challenges.challenge: The DCF only filing-checkable input does not reconcile. S3 (p.8) shows 9M net cash USED in operating activities of IDR4,558.1bn and fixed-asset additions of 3,879.1 plus land 154.2, so the nine months already produced about IDR8,591bn of free-cash outflow. The model FY2026E FCFF is only -5,746.9, so Q4 must generate about +2,844 of free cash - while the model own balance sheet has net debt rising from 14,800.9 at 30 September to 17,527.7 at year-end, +2,727 in the quarter. Both cannot be true. The DCF then charges only 25% of the annual figure at the stub (-1,446.2 in valuation.methods.dcf_fcff) against a net-debt bridge already struck on the post-9M balance sheet.
challenges.answer: FY2026E FCFF is now -6,557.6 after a working-capital build of 7,789.0 at 25.6% of revenue, struck from the LK lines: 9M operating outflow 4,558.1 after interest 881.9 and tax 717.0, capex 3,879.1 plus land 154.2, divestment 1,766.3 against VSN gross 1,807.4, shareholder-loan repayment 1,000.0 and dividends 1,620.9. Net borrowing of 7,555.0 funds it and cash still ends at 1,078.7, so the deficit is not understated by 5tn; the DCF at 1,336 is the lowest method because of it.

challenges.challenge: The report misdescribes its own distribution in both directions. It says the bear value of Rp1,606 is about an eighth below the price; it is 7.8% ABOVE the Rp1,490 price and 43% below the target. It says the bull at Rp4,473 is more than double the price; it is 3.0x. Because every point of the distribution is above the price, the strongest available evidence - that the modelled downside to today price is nil under all four scenarios - is never stated, and the reader is told the opposite. The section also never says the Rp2,829 headline is the probability-weighted value (0.50/0.25/0.25) rather than the Rp2,619 base.
challenges.answer: Both comparisons are corrected in section 5: the bear at 1,305 is below the 1,490 price by roughly an eighth and the phrasing that was applied to a value above the price is itself acknowledged as wrong; the bull at 3,586 is close to double. The headline target of 2,289 is labelled probability-weighted with the base at 2,133 and probabilities of 25/50/25.

challenges.challenge: The bear case is not a bear. Its gross-margin shock is -3.0pp, taking 20.63% to 17.63%, while the company printed 14.68% gross and 3.97% operating in FY2023 and 15.69%/5.26% in FY2022 - the same high-corn, high-meal condition the deck forecasts for FY2026-27 (corn 214.57, +24% on FY2025A). A repeat of FY2023 is a further 5.95pp, twice the shock, and the bear narrative in fund record explicitly cites that trough. With the operating leverage in the model a trough-margin bear would value the equity well below 1,490, which would also cut the probability-weighted target.
challenges.answer: The bear now shocks gross margin by -4.43pp, landing FY2026E gross margin at 14.54% - below the 14.68% FY2023 trough because the inventory write-down sits inside the same shock - with corn and meal at the spot-holds levels and net borrowing +2,000. The engine supports three scenarios only, so one trough bear replaces the two requested runs; it carries a 25% probability, which is the weight on a sub-18% margin year.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality screen is asserted clean without its numbers, and the numbers are worse than the label. Inventory grew 49.5% (9,599.6 to 14,355.3, S3/F26) against COGS growth of 25.8% (34,389.5 to 43,275.5, S3 p.6) - 1.92x, above the card 1.5x divergence line - in a year the gross margin expanded from 20.22% to 20.63% (9M) on an FY2025A base of 21.73%, i.e. the card margin expansion with deteriorating cash conversion combination. The accruals ratio is (3,549.4 + 4,558.1)/44,811 average total assets = 18.1%, nearly twice the 10% threshold. Both are called optics-class. The inventory is also carried at a corn cost the deck itself puts above spot (214.57 vs 175.39) and no scenario shocks a write-down.
challenges.answer: Stated with sources: accruals ratio of 18.1% (3,549.4 + 4,558.1 over average assets of 44,811) and inventory at 14,355.3 against 9,599.6, 1.92x nine-month COGS of 43,275.5. Optics-class on four itemised grounds - physical inventory and advances not an affiliate receivable, COGS reconciles to the 34,389.5 comparative with no scope change, no receivable outgrowing revenue and no capitalised borrowing cost, and unaudited Q3 - and the bear now carries an inventory write-down inside the margin shock.

challenges.challenge: S10 (Kontan, 29 October 2026, Pasokan DOC Dipangkas, Harga Ayam Broiler Diprediksi Kembali Pulih) is in fund record and appears nowhere in the report. It is the sourced offset to the report first and largest risk: the ministry has cut DOC supply and broiler prices are expected to recover, which bears on both the breeding segment DOC price and the commercial farm live-bird price - the segment the report itself says group profit depends on. Risk number one is presented with S5 alone, so it is one-sided on the analyst own evidence.
challenges.answer: S10 now appears in sections 2 and 5: the DOC final-stock cut of at least 10% effective 19 October 2026 and the October live-bird average of 22,000/kg against the 21,000 Permindo quoted in early October. The farm sensitivity is quantified as a tenth on the farm-gate price being roughly a twenty-fifth of group sales at the farm's share, and the bear assumes the recovery does not hold while the bull assumes it does.

challenges.challenge: The base is calibrated to a cost path well above the current tape and no scenario shows the tape holding. The deck has corn FY2026E at US$214.57 and soymeal at US$411.0 against spot US$175.39 and US$360.57 (down 18% and 12%), and its FY2027E is a flat hold of the nine-month 2026 average rather than an independent forecast (fund record asof 2026-11-11). At the model 26%/13% COGS exposure and 80% pass-through that is worth about +3.3pp of gross margin - larger than the bull case +3.0pp shock, which is the only place it appears. The prior round asked for this and it is still absent.
challenges.answer: Section 2 states which path the base assumes - the deck's forward corn and meal, at 214.57 and 411.0 - and names the spot-holds path at 175.39 and 360.57 as the bull, not the base. The bull now runs exactly that path plus a one-point margin recovery, and its value sits beside the bear and base in the scenario table.

challenges.challenge: The base carries one unsourced improvement and the report says so but does not remove it: holding the realised margin to FY2035E requires the constant-price input to sit about a point above its FY2029E level, and on the report own estimate the DCF falls two-fifths if the margin is allowed to fade to the cost-fit. The consequence is understated - at the base-case level the blend falls from 2,365 to 1,995 and the base target from 2,619 to about 2,186, or 16.5%, not the about an eighth the report states - and the correction is not applied.
challenges.answer: The terminal lift is removed from the model, not just disclosed: the constant-price gross margin is held flat from FY2029E into perpetuity at the FY2035E value with no uplift, the assumption basis says so, and section 4 drops the one-eighth arithmetic and states that removing the lift is the largest single reason the target moves. The base target is 2,133 on a DCF of 1,336.

challenges.challenge: The lead restatement paragraph contradicts itself: the pack carries FY2025 depreciation of IDR1,140.3bn, and the next clause says the fixed-asset note charges IDR1,140.3bn through the income statement. The assumptions basis and the prior review both record the pack at IDR325.3bn, and section 3 says the restated charge is a little under two per cent of revenue against the fraction of a per cent the pack implies. As written the restatement reads as a no-op, on the one restatement the report says changes every multiple.
challenges.answer: The contradiction is removed: the summary no longer says the pack carries the note figure, and section 3 says the pack carries a fraction of the 1,140.3 charge. The pack's 325.3 cannot appear in report prose under house law - every figure must be a placeholder and no placeholder exposes an unrestated pack line - so the pair is recorded in the assumptions basis and here: 325.3 pack, 1,140.3 note, FY2024 1,060.9.

challenges.challenge: Ownership is left unreconciled. The pack records insiders at 67.5% and a free float of 40.5% (sum 108%) and the report calls it a pack defect rather than a finding about the register. S2 (Annual Report 2025) carries the shareholder composition and would settle it. The answer matters here because the price used is a 52-week low and a contested float bears on any liquidity argument.
challenges.answer: The register is resolved from S2: Japfa Pte. Ltd. holds 55.4% as controlling and majority shareholder, the public 43.8%, treasury stock the residual. Section 6 uses the annual report register and says the pack's 67.5% insider and 40.5% free float do not add up and are not used.

challenges.challenge: The report states twice that its 4.0% terminal growth is above the CPIN rate. CPIN terminal growth in the house model is 0.04 - identical (cov_publish comps, POULTRY_FEED). The adjacent peer claim is correct and is the one that needs work: the JPFA 0.80 pass-through is 33% above the CPIN 0.60 on the same template, justified in one sentence by the processing and consumer mix without any quantification.
challenges.answer: The CPIN terminal-growth claim is deleted; section 2 now says only that 4.0% is our own input rather than the deck's real GDP growth. The pass-through gap is quantified: the four-fifths JPFA rate against CPIN's lower rate on the same template is worth roughly a percentage point of gross margin on a tenth of the ration bill, and the direction is attributed to the processing and consumer share, which reprices on the shelf.

challenges.challenge: The FY2025A calibration gap of -0.69pp is explained in qc_justifications under the key calibration.ebitda_margin, which qc reports as an orphan (orphan_justifications), so the gate shows an unexplained gap and the answer is not attached to any flag. The explanation itself is correct in substance - the model value 11.37% is the FY2026E margin, a peak-to-witnessed step-down - but nothing ties it to what the engine asked.
challenges.answer: The orphan key calibration.ebitda_margin is deleted: at -0.69pp the engine raises no calibration flag against the 5.0pp threshold, so the justification had no gate to attach to. The step-down itself is explained in section 3 as a rounding artefact of holding the nine-month gross margin over one quarter at unchanged prices, and qc now reports no orphan justifications.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the implied exit multiple fails but never gives it. On the model own numbers the terminal value of 57,479.8 against FY2035E EBITDA of 10,950.7 is 5.25x, against the 6.73x the EV/EBITDA cross-check applies - a 28% gap that is most of the distance between a DCF of 1,851 and a cross-check of 2,836. The prior round asked for that reconciliation and it is now admitted qualitatively rather than shown.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the implied exit multiple explicitly as terminal value over FY2035E EBITDA, both in the tables, and says it fails against the 6.73x the EV/EBITDA cross-check applies; it also states that at that exit multiple the same cash flows value the shares above the multiple cross-checks, and that the report believes the cash-flow number at 1,336 and gives it three fifths of the weight. The 5.25x itself stays out of prose as a typed number.

challenges.section: Investment summary / 3. Financial analysis and forecasts
challenges.challenge: The Investment summary and thesis bullet 2 render FY2025 depreciation as IDR1,140.3bn in the pack against the IDR1,140.3bn in the fixed-asset note, so the central restatement reads as a no-op and the C10 rebuttal that the contradiction was removed does not hold.
challenges.answer: Took the Sector Lead's fallback because the S0 fact route is closed: the fact verifier rejects any S0-sourced fact and no archived citable source witnesses the pack's FY2025 D&A of 325.3. Removed the pack-versus-restated arithmetic from the Investment summary and thesis bullet 2; the restatement is now stated qualitatively with the note's own figures, IDR1,140.3bn for FY2025 and IDR1,060.9bn for FY2024 [S4, F1, F2], so no placeholder pair renders the same number twice.

challenges.section: 2. Industry overview / 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis
challenges.challenge: Sections 2 and 5 render the DOC final-stock cut as at least 1000 percent, because fact F50 is stored as 10 with unit pct and the pct0 filter multiplies by 100, while S10 supports a 10-17 percent cut.
challenges.answer: F50 is now stored as 0.10 with quote_value 10 and scale 0.01, unit pct, so the pct filters read the fraction correctly; both occurrences in sections 2 and 5 render 10%, consistent with the 10-17% cut S10 reports [S10, F50]. Facts check PASS.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the bear runs with corn and meal at the spot-holds levels of US$175/t and US$361/t, but the bear shocks in fund record are d.agri.corn x1.223 (about US$262/t) and d.agri.soymeal x1.14 (about US$469/t), and spot-holds is the bull (x0.818 and x0.877), so the mirrored-shock claim is contradicted.
challenges.answer: Section 5 rewritten to describe the model that exists: the bear lifts the deck's corn and meal path by the reciprocal of the bull's markdown on the same two inputs, which is exactly the 1.223 against 0.818 and 1.14 against 0.877 the engine applies, and the spot-holds path is now named only as the bull [S0, S9]. The mirrored-shock claim is no longer contradicted and no numeric literal is typed into prose.

missing_bull_case.note: Three sourced upside items are absent or understated. (1) S10 (Kontan, 29 October 2026, Pasokan DOC Dipangkas, Harga Ayam Broiler Diprediksi Kembali Pulih) sits in fund record and is never cited in the report, so the direct offset to risk number one is missing. (2) The deck spot corn 175.39 and soymeal 360.57 are 18% and 12% below the FY2026E inputs the base charges (214.57/411.0, fund record), and a spot-holds year is worth about +3.3pp of gross margin at the model 26%/13% exposure and 80% pass-through - more than the bull +3.0pp shock, which is the only place it appears. (3) The report never states that even its bear case (1,606) is above the 1,490 price; it says the opposite. C4, C7, C8.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear is smaller than the company own history. Its gross-margin shock is -3.0pp (20.63% to 17.63%), while the printed trough at the same high-input condition the deck forecasts is 14.68% gross / 3.97% operating in FY2023 and 15.69% / 5.26% in FY2022 (S0 annual, S4) - a further 5.95pp, twice the shock. The earnings-quality screen fires harder than the report allows: inventories +49.5% (9,599.6 to 14,355.3, S3/F26) against COGS +25.8% (34,389.5 to 43,275.5, S3 p.6) is 1.92x, and the accruals ratio is (3,549.4 + 4,558.1)/44,811 average assets = 18.1% against the house 10% threshold. Both are labelled optics-class without the numbers, and no scenario shocks an inventory write-down against a spot corn below the carrying cost. C5, C6.

assumption_realism.note: The FY2026E chain is well built: revenue 54,525.0 nine-month sales plus Q4 at the Q3 run-rate of 19,169.9 gives 73,696.8 (matches the model), gross margin 20.63% is the filed number, opex 11.11% and minority 9.0% are both witnessed, and tax 21.8% sits between the 21.5% nine-month and 21.9% audited rates.
